verdict.summary: Creating and testing an OAuth app for your own HubSpot account is quick, but new apps must be built with the Projects-based platform and HubSpot CLI because the legacy app UI can no longer create public apps. Installs by other accounts need no HubSpot review, but a Marketplace listing is a manual review, and certification needs 6 months of listing and 60 active installs.
verdict.hands_on_effort: Gate 1 and 2: about half a day of setup, plus domain verification if you want to drop the unverified-app warning. Gate 3 (Marketplace listing): several days of preparation, then a review wait. Certification is a separate later project.
verdict.time_to_first_connection: Under an hour once the Projects app is created and uploaded (estimate; depends on developer account setup).
verdict.approval_wait: None for your own account or for unlisted installs. Marketplace listing: initial review within 10 business days, full cycle up to 60 days from feedback. Certification: only after 6 months listed with 60 active installs.

gates.name: Own account (development use)
gates.unlocks: Create the app, configure OAuth, and connect your own HubSpot account through the authorization flow.
limits: Legacy public app creation is closed; new apps use the Projects platform and HubSpot CLI.
Access tokens expire after 1800 seconds (30 minutes) per the legacy quickstart; refresh is required.
Install requires a HubSpot account where you hold Super Admin rights, or HubSpot Marketplace Access permission.
gates.time_to_reach: Minutes to about an hour after the developer account exists.

gates.name: Unlisted public app (other accounts, no HubSpot review)
gates.unlocks: Other HubSpot accounts can install the app through the OAuth authorize link. HubSpot does not review unlisted apps.
limits: Unverified apps show a warning. The installer must review every scope, type 'I accept the risk', and click Connect.
A verified domain shows its name with a banner saying HubSpot has not reviewed or approved the app.
Only one verified domain is allowed per account, shared by all of that account's apps.
No official install cap for unlisted apps was found.
A community post reports that the unreviewed warning cannot be removed by technical review (not an official policy).
gates.time_to_reach: Immediately after Gate 1 for unverified installs. A verified domain adds a DNS TXT verification step.

gates.name: Marketplace listing (public, reviewed)
gates.unlocks: Public Marketplace listing with no unverified or unreviewed banner. Certification is a further step that unlocks certified status.
limits: Listing requires OAuth as the sole authorization method and a single OAuth client ID tied to the listing.
At least three active, unique installs are required for the listing.
Only one app can be submitted for listing review at a time; other submissions are rejected automatically.
HubSpot can refuse or unpublish a listing at its discretion.
Listing requires agreement to the Technology Partner Program Agreement. Certification has no fee and no revenue share.
gates.time_to_reach: Listing review: initial review within 10 business days; full review and feedback cycle up to 60 days. Certification: 6+ months listed and 60+ active installs before you can apply.

steps.title: Decide between Composio managed OAuth and your own HubSpot app
steps.detail: Composio ships a managed HubSpot OAuth config, so you can start there for a Composio-brokered connection. Register your own HubSpot app if you need your own redirect URI or branding, or if you plan to list on the Marketplace. A Marketplace listing requires your own OAuth client ID.
gotchas: Composio's default scope list is broad. It includes Enterprise-only scopes and several names not confirmed on HubSpot's scope reference. Trim it before use.

steps.title: Create the developer account and a Projects-based app
steps.detail: Sign in to or create a HubSpot developer account. Do not use the legacy app creation UI, because it can no longer create new public apps. Create a Projects app with the HubSpot CLI and use the Projects-based tooling.
gotchas: Developer account prerequisites (paid vs free, Super Admin requirement, business verification) were not confirmed by an official page.

steps.title: Declare scopes and redirect URL in app-hsmeta.json
steps.detail: Draft the auth block of the app's app-hsmeta.json with the scopes you actually use and the redirect URL. Put scopes that apply only to some accounts in the optional or conditionally required sets, not the required set. Use https for production URLs.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

values.label: Scope rule
values.value: Request only scopes the app uses; the oauth scope is added by default

gotchas: Any scope checked as required in the Auth settings must be present in the scope parameter, or the authorize page errors.
Production redirect URIs must use https. http works only for localhost testing. IP addresses are not supported as hosts.

steps.title: Upload the app and read the client ID and secret
steps.detail: Run the HubSpot CLI upload command for the project (hs project upload). Then open the app's settings and go to the Auth page to copy the client ID and client secret.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Store the client secret in your secret manager, not in source control.

steps.title: Build the authorization URL
steps.detail: Build the authorize link with client_id, redirect_uri, and a space-separated scope list. Add state for CSRF protection. optional_scope is optional.

steps.title: Run a test install and exchange the code for tokens
steps.detail: Open the authorize link while signed in to a HubSpot account where you are Super Admin, and click Connect. HubSpot redirects back with a code. Exchange it at the token endpoint with grant_type authorization_code, the code, redirect_uri, client_id, and client_secret.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: Users must authorize with the OAuth authorization code flow. Copying and pasting codes or tokens is prohibited for listed apps.

steps.title: Check OAuth events in the Logs
steps.detail: Confirm the install in Development > Monitoring > Logs. The log shows authorization requests, grants, code expiry, and token exchange. Use it to debug failed installs.

steps.title: Implement token refresh before the 30-minute expiry
steps.detail: Store the refresh token and refresh the access token before it expires. The legacy quickstart uses POST to the token endpoint with grant_type refresh_token. The Marketplace requires apps to refresh tokens without user involvement.
gotchas: The Projects docs use /oauth/v3/token for code exchange and the legacy quickstart uses /oauth/v1/token. Confirm the refresh endpoint against the current docs before shipping.

steps.title: Add a verified domain (optional, for Gate 2)
steps.detail: In the app's Contact & support settings, add a DNS TXT record to verify your domain. Verified apps show the domain and a banner, instead of the unverified warning. Only one verified domain is allowed per account.
gotchas: The verified domain is re-checked periodically. A verified domain does not remove the 'not reviewed or approved' banner.

steps.title: Test an install from a second HubSpot account
steps.detail: Install from a HubSpot account that is not yours to see what other users see. Review the scope list, type 'I accept the risk', and click Connect. Confirm the callback works and the token exchange succeeds.
gotchas: Unverified apps show a separate warning from verified ones. Plan your install instructions for both.

steps.title: Prepare the Marketplace listing package
steps.detail: Prepare a verified domain, a live setup documentation URL, privacy policy and terms-of-service URLs, a support contact, an install button URL, and a Shared data table that matches the requested scopes. Agree to the Technology Partner Program Agreement. Remove any scopes the app does not use.
gotchas: Listing submissions missing required fields are set to Draft. Apps must not require another public or private app to function.

steps.title: Submit the listing and wait for review
steps.detail: Submit the listing from the developer account. Only one app can be in listing review at a time. The Ecosystem Quality team reviews it manually; the initial review is within 10 business days.
gotchas: Listing needs at least three active, unique installs.

steps.title: Apply for certification after 6 months and 60 installs
steps.detail: Once the app is listed for at least 6 months with 60 active installs, go to Development > App Listings > More > Certify app. Paste a YouTube demo URL in the dialog. The video must be at least three minutes and show install, configuration, core use, disconnect, and uninstall.
steps.est_time: 1-2 days to record and edit the demo
gotchas: Certified apps must call the Uninstall App API when a customer removes the app.
If certification fails, you can re-apply after six months. HubSpot will not notify you when you become eligible.

requirements.item: Create the app in the Projects platform, not the legacy UI
requirements.detail: Legacy public app creation is closed for new apps. New apps use the HubSpot CLI with Projects-based tooling.
Installing requires Super Admin rights or the HubSpot Marketplace Access permission.
http is allowed only for localhost testing. IP addresses are not supported as hosts.
Access tokens expire after 30 minutes in the legacy quickstart. Refresh with grant_type refresh_token. Marketplace apps must refresh without user involvement.
Unverified apps show a warning. Installers must review every scope, type 'I accept the risk', and click Connect.
Verified via DNS TXT record in Contact & support settings. One verified domain per account, shared by all of that account's apps.
Certification requires a verified domain, a security assessment of outdated software and web-server issues, and a questionnaire on encryption, access controls, and token lifecycle.
OAuth as the sole authorization method, a single OAuth client ID tied to the listing, and at least three active unique installs.
Verified domain, live setup documentation, privacy policy and terms-of-service URLs, support contact, install button URL, and a Shared data table matching the requested scopes.
Every scope requested in required or optional_scope must be used. Extraneous scopes must be removed. Scopes that apply only to some users belong in the conditionally required or optional sets.
Users must authorize through the OAuth authorization code flow. Copying and pasting codes or tokens is prohibited.
Certified apps must call the Uninstall App API when a customer removes the app.
100 inbound requests every 10 seconds per connected account. Certification also requires an average success rate above 95%, counting error responses.
Active installs are unique HubSpot production accounts, unaffiliated with your organization, with successful app activity in the past 30 days.
Listed for at least 6 months and at least 60 active unique installs to apply, and to keep certified status.
At least three minutes, with audio or text, showing install, configuration, core use, disconnect, and uninstall. Promotional sales videos are rejected. Only one app in certification at a time.
Apps built on a developer-platform version that HubSpot has declared unsupported cannot be listed.
No fee to list or certify, and no revenue share.

scopes.effect: Added by default to all apps. You do not need to request it.
Custom-object scopes are tied to Enterprise accounts only. Installs from non-Enterprise accounts will not get this scope. Composio default list includes it.
Custom-object schema scope; Enterprise-only per the custom-object scope rule. Composio default list includes it.

scopes.scope: Sensitive and highly sensitive CRM scopes (e.g. some crm.* object scopes)
scopes.effect: Several sensitive and highly sensitive CRM scopes are tied to Enterprise accounts only. Check each scope on the scope reference before you request it.
Being replaced by granular scopes such as files.read. HubSpot recommends migrating to the granular scopes.
Included in the Composio default list but not confirmed on HubSpot's scope reference. Verify before requesting.

blockers.symptom: The legacy Developer Platform UI does not let you create a new public app.
blockers.cause: Creation of legacy public apps was disabled May 26, 2026 (accounts created on or after that date) and June 23, 2026 (older accounts).
blockers.fix: Create the app with the HubSpot CLI using the Projects-based tooling, and declare scopes in app-hsmeta.json.

blockers.symptom: Other accounts see a warning and must type 'I accept the risk' to install.
blockers.cause: The app is unverified and unlisted. HubSpot does not review unlisted apps.
blockers.fix: Verify a domain (one per account) to show a banner instead. Listing on the Marketplace removes both banners but requires review.

blockers.symptom: Marketplace submission is rejected or stays in Draft.
blockers.cause: Required listing fields are missing (verified domain, legal URLs, support contact, install URL, Shared data table), or the app has fewer than three active unique installs.
blockers.fix: Complete every listing field, make the Shared data table match the scopes, and reach three active installs before submitting.

blockers.symptom: Listing review rejects the app for extra scopes.
blockers.cause: The app requests scopes it does not use.
blockers.fix: Remove unused scopes from required and optional_scope. Move scopes that only some accounts need into the conditionally required or optional sets.

blockers.symptom: Certification request is cancelled or the app is removed from the Marketplace.
blockers.cause: Fewer than 60 active unique installs, or the average success rate is below 95%.
blockers.fix: Keep at least 60 active installs and monitor success rate, counting error responses. Respect 100 requests per 10 seconds per account.

blockers.symptom: Authorize page errors for a scope.
blockers.cause: A scope checked as required in the Auth settings is missing from the scope parameter.
blockers.fix: Add every required scope to the scope list in the authorize URL, or uncheck it in Auth settings.

blockers.symptom: Users get signed out or API calls fail after about 30 minutes.
blockers.cause: Access tokens expire after 30 minutes (legacy quickstart value).
blockers.fix: Refresh the access token before expiry using grant_type refresh_token, and store the new refresh token.

composio.note: Start on Composio managed OAuth for a Composio-brokered connection. Its default redirect is Composio's own backend. Bring your own HubSpot public app when you need your own redirect URI or branding, or when you plan to list on the Marketplace, since the listing needs its own OAuth client ID. Trim the default scope list before relying on it: it includes Enterprise-only scopes (crm.objects.custom.read, crm.schemas.custom.read) and several names not confirmed on HubSpot's scope reference (accounting, tickets, timeline, e-commerce, content).

open_questions: Developer account prerequisites are unconfirmed: free vs paid, whether Super Admin is needed to create the developer account, business verification, and partner-program enrollment.
No official install cap was found for an unlisted, unreviewed public app. The only numeric thresholds are the three-install listing minimum and the 60-install certification minimum.
No official timeline was found for approval of an unlisted public app. The 10-business-day and 60-day timelines apply to listing and certification only.

Refresh endpoint is unclear: the Projects docs use /oauth/v3/token for code exchange, while the legacy quickstart uses /oauth/v1/token for refresh. The 30-minute token lifetime comes from the legacy quickstart. Confirm both against the current Projects OAuth quickstart, which was not fetched.
Scope names not confirmed on HubSpot's scope reference: accounting, tickets, timeline, e-commerce, content (from Composio's default list). Verify before requesting.
PKCE support is unverified. The only source is a third-party blog saying HubSpot does not support PKCE.
Rejection behavior for an invalid client_id is unconfirmed. An authorize probe returned a 200 HTML page, not a standard OAuth error redirect.
The community claim that a public app's unreviewed warning cannot be removed by technical review is not an official policy. Confirm with HubSpot before relying on it.
Whether a Composio-brokered connection can use the managed app for a Marketplace listing is not covered. The listing requires your own single OAuth client ID.
